documents.title: M2023.11.28 Motion to Recommend Adoption of AI Policy
documents.stance_why: The motion has instructors "set their own policies" in their courses, but also states that students are "prohibited" from using generative AI "unless given explicit permission". Because the permission rests on each instructor, it sets no tiers and hands the decision to instructors. It does set a university-wide ban-by-default and a disclosure rule, so restrict is the other candidate, but the instructor discretion sentence comes first and frames the whole policy.
documents.summary: A Faculty Senate motion recommending a university-wide AI policy. Instructors set their own course rules and put them in the syllabus. Unless an instructor gives explicit permission, students may not use generative AI for exams or assignments. Notable AI use must be acknowledged, and students who are unsure must ask. The PDF leaves the vote blank, so adoption is not confirmed.

units.resolution_why: Coder A coded P01, coder B coded P06 (plus a separate P22 exam unit). The source says 'Students are prohibited from employing generative AI tools to complete exams or assignments ... unless given explicit permission from their course instructor.' This bans AI on graded work by default with an explicit-permission exception, which is P01. P06 is the rule for a silent syllabus, and the passage says nothing about silence; the instructor-permission clause is the exception inside the default ban. B's separate exam unit repeats the same sentence and the same rule, so it is dropped and exams are noted in the fit_note.
